<!-- slide 66 -->
## Building a Plot · Step 1 — The Canvas {.smaller}

[The Python viz stack · building a figure]{.eyebrow}

### 1 · Canvas

Every matplotlib plot starts with a **figure** (the page) and an **axes** (the panel you draw on). Nothing is plotted yet, you have only declared the surface.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "3"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 4.4
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 4.4))   # one figure, one axes
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 67 -->
## Building a Plot · Step 2 — Load & Plot Data {.smaller}

[The Python viz stack · building a figure]{.eyebrow}

### 2 · Data

Load the demo dataset and drop it onto the canvas with `ax.scatter()`. Default colour, default size, the shape of the data is now visible.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "2,4,7"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 4.4
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from genomics_course.data import load_scatter_demo

df = load_scatter_demo()                       # 120 genes: log2fc, expression, group

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 4.4))
ax.scatter(df.log2fc, df.expression, color=GREY, s=45, alpha=.75)   # the points
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 68 -->
## Building a Plot · Step 3 — Colour by Group {.smaller}

[The Python viz stack · building a figure]{.eyebrow}

### 3 · Colour

Loop over the groups, one pass each, one palette colour each. The two conditions separate visually.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "7-10"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 4.4
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from genomics_course.data import load_scatter_demo

df = load_scatter_demo()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 4.4))
for name, c in zip(["Control", "Treatment"], [GREEN, AMBER]):   # one colour each
    sub = df[df.group == name]
    ax.scatter(sub.log2fc, sub.expression, label=name, color=c, s=45, alpha=.75)
ax.legend(frameon=False)                     # name the groups
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 69 -->
## Building a Plot · Step 4 — Polish & Labels {.smaller}

[The Python viz stack · building a figure]{.eyebrow}

### 4 · Polish

A trend line, axis labels, and a title turn a scatter into a figure someone can read without you in the room.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "3,12-14,16-18"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 4.4
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from genomics_course.data import load_scatter_demo
from scipy.stats import linregress            # for the trend line

df = load_scatter_demo()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 4.4))
for name, c in zip(["Control", "Treatment"], [GREEN, AMBER]):
    sub = df[df.group == name]
    ax.scatter(sub.log2fc, sub.expression, label=name, color=c, s=45, alpha=.75)

b, a, *_ = linregress(df.log2fc, df.expression)   # fit y = b*x + a
xs = np.linspace(df.log2fc.min(), df.log2fc.max(), 100)
ax.plot(xs, b * xs + a, color=INK, lw=1.5, ls="--")   # draw the fit

ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold change")            # tell the reader the axes
ax.set_ylabel("expression")
ax.set_title("Control vs Treatment", color="#333333")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 70 -->
## Building a Plot · Step 5 — Style Once, Reuse Everywhere {.smaller}

[The Python viz stack · building a figure]{.eyebrow}

### 5 · House style

Bundle your spine and grid choices into one style block. Apply it and the per-axes polish disappears, every plot inherits the same look.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "6-13"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 4.4
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from genomics_course.data import load_scatter_demo

df = load_scatter_demo()

house = {                                    # define the house style ONCE
    "axes.spines.top":   False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid":         True,
    "grid.linestyle":    "--",
    "grid.color":        LINE,
}
with plt.rc_context(house):                  # apply it: no per-axes polish below
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 4.4))
    for name, c in zip(["Control", "Treatment"], [GREEN, AMBER]):
        sub = df[df.group == name]
        ax.scatter(sub.log2fc, sub.expression, label=name, color=c, s=45, alpha=.75)
    ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold change")
    ax.set_ylabel("expression")
    ax.set_title("styled once, applies everywhere", color="#333333")
    ax.legend(frameon=False)
plt.show()
```

::: {.takeaway}
[The bottom line]{.tl}
Build a figure in layers: **canvas → data → colour → polish**. Then lift the polish into a **style block you set once**, so every later plot starts publication-ready instead of being hand-tuned.
:::


<!-- slide 71 -->
## Common Plot Types in Matplotlib & Seaborn {.plot-slide background-color="#f6f4ee"}

[The Python viz stack]{.eyebrow}

### Eight common artists at a glance

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5

np.random.seed(42)
cats  = ['A','B','C','D']
vals  = [23, 45, 31, 58]
x_sc  = np.random.normal(0, 1, 150)
y_sc  = 0.7*x_sc + np.random.normal(0, 0.6, 150)
g_sc  = np.random.choice(['Ctrl','Treat'], 150)
ts    = np.arange(50)
tsv   = np.cumsum(np.random.normal(0.2, 1, 50))
bx    = [np.random.normal(m, 1.2, 60) for m in [3, 5, 4, 6]]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(12, 5.5), constrained_layout=True)

# Bar
axes[0,0].bar(cats, vals, color=[BRAND, ACCENT_YLW, BRAND_LIGHT, ACCENT_PURP])
axes[0,0].set_title('ax.bar()\nComparisons', fontsize=9)

# Scatter
for g, c in zip(['Ctrl','Treat'], [BRAND, RED]):
    m = g_sc == g
    axes[0,1].scatter(x_sc[m], y_sc[m], color=c, s=18, alpha=0.6, label=g)
axes[0,1].legend(fontsize=7); axes[0,1].set_title('ax.scatter()\nRelationships', fontsize=9)

# Line
axes[0,2].plot(ts, tsv, color=BRAND, linewidth=2)
axes[0,2].fill_between(ts, tsv, alpha=0.15, color=BRAND)
axes[0,2].set_title('ax.plot()\nTime series', fontsize=9)

# Hist
axes[0,3].hist(np.random.normal(50, 10, 500), bins=25, color=BRAND, alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white')
axes[0,3].set_title('ax.hist()\nDistributions', fontsize=9)

# Box
bp = axes[1,0].boxplot(bx, patch_artist=True, medianprops={'color':'white','linewidth':2})
for patch, c in zip(bp['boxes'], [BRAND, ACCENT_YLW, BRAND_LIGHT, ACCENT_PURP]):
    patch.set_facecolor(c); patch.set_alpha(0.7)
axes[1,0].set_title('ax.boxplot()\nDistributions', fontsize=9)

# Heatmap (seaborn)
mat = np.random.randn(8, 8)
sns.heatmap(mat, ax=axes[1,1], cmap='RdYlGn', center=0, linewidths=0.3,
            cbar_kws={'shrink': 0.7})
axes[1,1].set_title('sns.heatmap()\nExpression', fontsize=9)

# Violin
vp = axes[1,2].violinplot(bx, showmedians=True)
for pc, c in zip(vp['bodies'], [BRAND, ACCENT_YLW, BRAND_LIGHT, ACCENT_PURP]):
    pc.set_facecolor(c); pc.set_alpha(0.7)
axes[1,2].set_title('ax.violinplot()\nDensity', fontsize=9)

# Pairplot placeholder
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
axes[1,3].add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((0.05,0.05), 0.9, 0.9,
                    boxstyle='round', facecolor=BRAND+'22', edgecolor=BRAND))
axes[1,3].text(0.5, 0.5, 'sns.pairplot()\nMultivariate', ha='center', va='center',
               fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', color=BRAND, transform=axes[1,3].transAxes)
axes[1,3].set_xlim(0,1); axes[1,3].set_ylim(0,1); axes[1,3].axis('off')

for ax in axes.flat:
    ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)

plt.suptitle('Common Plot Types', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.show()
```
